core_requests: github provider (core-owned v3lum/data/providers/github.json): add env alias V3LUM_GITHUB_TOKEN to key 'github' (P111 cond 4); extensions cannot add keys.

docs/KEYS.md (AR22/A15): document the GitHub key as a team machine-account or GitHub App token, fine-grained 'public repositories, read-only, no permissions'; doctor v2 (P337/WP25) should run GithubUser.health_check() whose self-test refuses classic tokens with a non-empty X-OAuth-Scopes header (P111 cond 4).

P334 quota book: a keyed/keyless (and per-resource core/search) budget for the github provider (60/h keyless per egress IP, 5,000/h keyed, search 10/min keyless, 30/min keyed); the provider quota schema has one window set per provider. Until then GitHubBudget in github_user.py enforces X-RateLimit-Remaining per runtime (shared by every GitHub REST module through github_budget(ctx)), not persisted across processes.
github provider http_profile: concurrency 1 (serial requests avoid GitHub secondary rate limits); github.json is core-owned.

HostLimiter: the effective min_interval of a host is the largest interval any module ever declared for it, so one module's politeness interval slows every module of that host for the whole process (a 6 s search interval would have slowed all api.github.com calls); consider per-module or per-resource intervals.

Pivot tags (or a GUARD-01 rule on relations mentioned_in_post / forwarded_from) so post-derived indicators of telegram_public are hostile-tagged for the P376 guard (P112 cond 7); the module contract has no way to tag a pivot entity.

Read-only ctx.case_entities() (or equivalent) so github_user can expand commit e-mails that match any case entity (P111 cond 7); modules see only the seeds (options.seed_tlp) and their provenance path.

P172/WP17: telegram_public uses v3lum.core.detect.extract_iocs until v3lum.core.ioc.extract lands; the new extractor should also return Telegram/Discord invites (the module keeps its own invite patterns meanwhile).

WP09: publish sanitize.scrub_text in docs/contract_additions/WP09.md so telegram_public can chain it after its own P112 scrubber; consider a core 'post text' scrubbing profile (PAN to BIN6+last4, CPF/e-mail/phone masking, leaked-record line dropping) shared with telegram_channel_watch (P357).

HTTP cache: support caching a module-sanitized representation of non-JSON bodies (sanitize_body handles JSON only), so P112's 1 h cache can survive the process without raw t.me HTML ever reaching http_cache.db (cond 4 vs cond 5).

http.classify(): strong anti-bot body fingerprints (e.g. 'captcha-delivery.com', 'cf-chl-') are matched anywhere in user-generated pages such as t.me/s previews; a CTI post quoting them would make the page BLOCKED and trip the t.me circuit for the run. Consider limiting body fingerprints to <head>/small pages or exempting providers flagged as user-generated content.

tests/test_links.py FIXTURE_VALUES (top-level core test) lacks telegram_handle (and other v2 handle types), so packs cannot declare telegram_handle templates without failing it; telegram_public uses an inline manual_link 'https://t.me/s/{user}' meanwhile.
